What Kite solves

Starting a Flutter project often means repeating the same setup: theme files, routers, error contracts, provider wiring, feature folders, API clients, and reusable UI. Kite turns those decisions into readable, versioned templates while keeping the generated code inside your project and under your control.

01

Project foundations

Material 3 themes, routing, shared states, core errors, results, Riverpod bootstrap, and project configuration.

02

Feature architecture

Generate feature-first Clean Architecture or MVC modules with compile-safe contracts and no invented business logic.

03

Reusable foundations

Add theme-aware buttons, cards, avatars, Riverpod infrastructure, and a production Dio client when the project needs them.

04

Safe evolution

Preview plans, detect conflicts, track generated checksums, preserve edits, and upgrade templates intentionally.

One CLI, focused generators

kite init

Initialize an existing Flutter project with Kite's shared app foundation.

kite --feat:clean dashboard

Create a feature-first Clean Architecture module.

kite --feat:mvc profile

Create a feature-first MVC module using manual Riverpod providers.

kite --widget "[button,card,avatar]"

Add reusable Material 3 components and their shared support files.

kite --state riverpod

Add production Riverpod bootstrap and async state helpers.

kite --api:dio

Add typed networking, token interception, exception mapping, and providers.

Generated code remains your code

Kite is deliberately not a runtime framework. It writes ordinary Dart and Flutter source that your team can read, review, refactor, and own. Template metadata is stored separately from template source, so architecture presets can evolve without turning Dart code into escaped JSON.

✓
Designed for professional ownership

Kite generates starting points and infrastructure—not fake API methods, business rules, or domain operations that your application never requested.
